item.title: China calls for more practical results with Pacific Island countries in police capacity building, cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 8 -- China is willing to work with Pacific Island countries to deepen the ministerial-level dialogue mechanism on police capacity building and cooperation, and strive to achieve more practical results, Chinese State Councilor and Minister of Public Security Wang Xiaohong said Tuesday. Wang made the remarks while delivering a speech at the fifth ministerial dialogue on police capacity building and cooperation between China and the Pacific Island countries in Beijing. Since the establishment of the ministerial dialogue mechanism, Wang said, the foundation of mutual trust between China and Pacific Island countries has grown stronger. Training and exchanges have deepened and solidified, law enforcement cooperation has been practical and effective, and police authorities have built closer bonds and greater mutual understanding. This has played a positive role in promoting regional prosperity, stability and development. Wang said that China stands ready to work with all parties to earnestly implement the important consensus reached by the leaders of China and Pacific Island countries, actively practice the four major global initiatives, adhere to openness and inclusiveness, strengthen multilateral cooperation, and make greater contributions to building a China-Pacific Island countries community with a shared future. Wang and Vanuatu's Minister of Internal Affairs Andrew Napuat co-chaired the ministerial dialogue. On the same day, Wang met separately with International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol) President Lucas Philippe, Interpol Secretary General Valdecy Urquiza, and Andrew Napuat.

item.title: Chinese premier calls for sustainable urban renewal
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 8 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Tuesday called for developing sustainable urban renewal models and optimizing the structure of urban areas nationwide. Li made the remarks while presiding over a State Council study session on advancing high-quality urban renewal. China has made significant progress in advancing new industrialization and urbanization in recent years, amid profound changes in population dynamics, growth drivers and the real estate market, Li said. Against this backdrop, urban renewal has become a key means of improving the living environment and people's well-being, driving domestic demand, and accelerating the transformation of growth drivers, he said. To ensure sustainable urban renewal, a people-centered approach must be upheld throughout the process, the premier said, adding that priority should go to making the most of revitalized public spaces, service facilities, and ecological resources to better meet people's needs. Highlighting the need to strengthen disaster prevention and mitigation capabilities, Li called for proactive efforts to guard against and respond to disasters such as floods, fires and earthquakes. Efforts should be made to promote renovation and upgrading at the levels of housing, neighborhoods, communities and urban areas, Li said. He also called for accelerating the transformation and upgrading of old districts and factory zones, and actively fostering new industries and business models. Li also emphasized the importance of developing distinctive urban characteristics while preserving cityscapes and historical heritage. Efforts should be intensified to step up government investment and ensure the coordinated and effective use of various policy funds, Li said, adding that credit support should be strengthened to establish a diversified and sustainable financing system. Policies, laws and regulations concerning planning, land use, fiscal and taxation matters, and finance should be optimized in a timely manner to align with the practical needs of urban renewal, Li added.

item.title: Xi extends congratulations over DPRK's 78th founding anniversary
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 9 -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and Chinese president, on Wednesday extended congratulations to Kim Jong Un, general secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea (WPK) and president of the State Affairs of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), over the DPRK's 78th founding anniversary. In his message, Xi pointed out that over the past 78 years, under the leadership of the WPK, the DPRK people have achieved vigorous development in various fields of socialist construction through self-reliance, unity and hard work. In recent years in particular, under the leadership of Kim, the WPK and the DPRK people have made every effort to advance economic and social development, scoring a series of development achievements to China's heartfelt delight, said Xi. Xi expressed confidence that the brotherly DPRK people will surely achieve the goals and tasks set forth at the Ninth Congress of the WPK and continuously open up new prospects for the cause of Party and state development. China and the DPRK are friendly socialist neighbors who stand by each other and share weal and woe, Xi said, stressing that it is an unswerving policy of the CPC and the Chinese government to preserve, consolidate and develop China-DPRK relations. Xi noted that in June this year, he paid a state visit to the DPRK and met with Kim again, opening a new chapter in the development of relations between the two Parties and the two countries. Xi said that he stands ready to work together with Kim to continue strengthening the strategic guidance of relations between the two Parties and the two countries, jointly promote the development of their respective Party and state causes, continuously improve the well-being of the two peoples and deepen their friendship, so as to make greater contributions to promoting peace, stability, development and prosperity in the region and the world at large.

item.title: China stresses development of high-quality textbook system as new semester begins
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
BEIJING, Sept. 8 -- Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang on Tuesday called for accelerating the development of a high-quality textbook system with Chinese characteristics, as schools across the country started a new academic semester. Ding, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, made the remarks at a national conference on textbook work held in Beijing. He emphasized the need to fully understand the political, people-centered and strategic nature of education, and to strengthen and improve textbook development with a strong sense of political responsibility and historical mission. Efforts should be made to speed up the establishment of a high-quality textbook system with Chinese characteristics to provide strong support for building China into a leading country in education, Ding said. He highlighted the correct political direction and value orientation concerning textbooks and called for efforts to ensure that the Party's educational policies are implemented throughout all aspects of textbook development. Efforts should focus on fostering virtue through education and further incorporating the Party's innovative theories into courses and teaching materials. China should better adapt its textbook development to the requirements of the times and accelerate efforts to establish a Chinese intellectual system and an original textbook system in philosophy and social sciences, he noted. He also stressed stricter management of the compilation, review, publication and distribution of textbooks, as well as standardized procedures for their selection and use. The conference came as a new school year got underway across China. Primary and secondary schools and universities in many parts of the country welcomed students back to campuses in early September following the summer vacation. In 2025, China had 440,700 schools at all levels and of all types, with over 280.4 million students enrolled in education programs of various types, underscoring the scale of the country's textbook development and management endeavors. Ding's remarks also came amid a years-long national push to strengthen textbook work. The State Council established a national textbook committee in 2017, and all 31 provincial-level regions on the Chinese mainland subsequently set up provincial-level leading bodies for textbook work. Strengthening the creation and management of teaching materials was included in the report to the 20th CPC National Congress in 2022. The push was further highlighted in China's long-term education planning in 2026, when the State Council issued the 15th Five-Year Plan for education development. The plan called for implementing the state's responsibility for textbook development and comprehensively advancing the development of a high-quality textbook system with Chinese characteristics.

item.title: Xi holds phone talks with British PM
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
BEIJING, Sept. 8 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday held phone talks with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham. Congratulating Burnham on assuming office as British prime minister, Xi said that China and Britain are comprehensive strategic partners. Despite differences in their social systems and national conditions, the two countries share more common interests than differences. Xi urged the two sides to respect and trust each other, overcome differences, seek common ground and expand mutually beneficial cooperation. Both governments are committed to developing their economies and improving people's well-being, and the two countries can complement each other's strengths and facilitate each other's development, Xi said. During the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), China will further expand opening up in such areas as education, healthcare and finance, all of which offer great potential for bilateral cooperation, Xi said. Pointing out that China and Britain are both major countries in science and technology with rich resources in education, culture, sports and other fields, Xi called on the two sides to adopt an open and forward-looking approach and strengthen exchanges and cooperation in various fields. Xi expressed the hope that the British side will fully protect the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese investors. Xi noted that China and Britain, as permanent members of the UN Security Council and major economies in the world, both support multilateralism and open trade and uphold the central role of the United Nations. The two sides should strengthen communication and coordination within frameworks such as the United Nations, the Group of 20 and the World Trade Organization, and promote an equal and orderly multipolar world and a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, Xi said. Burnham agreed, saying that he had served as mayor of Manchester for many years and maintained friendly exchanges with China for years. President Xi's visit to Manchester during his state visit to Britain in 2015 had a significant impact on promoting local exchanges and cooperation with China, Burnham said. Burnham said Britain is willing to maintain continuity in its policy toward China and remain firmly committed to developing a long-term, stable strategic partnership between Britain and China. Britain is ready to conduct high-level exchanges with China, advance bilateral cooperation in various fields, strengthen people-to-people exchanges, and restore bilateral relations to their historic high, so as to better benefit the peoples of both countries, Burnham added. Burnham said that Britain's position on the Taiwan question remains unchanged. Amid the current turbulent and complex international landscape undergoing changes, Britain and China, as permanent members of the UN Security Council, should promote the resolution of international hotspot issues through dialogue, jointly address global challenges such as climate change, and work together to safeguard world stability and prosperity, Burnham added. Burnham spoke highly of China's efficient and effective response to the mudslide disaster that struck Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, and expressed appreciation for China's assistance to affected British citizens.

item.title: China releases 5-year development plan for information, communications sector
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
BEIJING, Sept. 7 -- China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology has issued a development plan for the information and communications industry during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) to promote the high-quality development of this sector. By 2030, a new-generation communications network with comprehensive coverage and leading performance is expected to be fully established, according to the plan, which has called for efforts to accelerate the development of a technologically advanced, secure and controllable information and communications industrial system. Meanwhile, an agile and efficient governance system integrating technology and management is expected to be effectively established, and network and data security capabilities featuring all-domain coordination and practical application will be significantly enhanced, the plan said. The industry's empowerment level and degree of globalization will be further improved, laying a solid foundation for basically achieving modernization of the information and communications sector by 2035, the plan added. The plan also outlines 13 key indicators, including achieving information and communications industry revenue of 4.1 trillion yuan (about 604.8 billion U.S. dollars) by 2030, cumulative investment of 3.8 trillion yuan in information infrastructure, and an average annual growth rate of 7 percent in total telecommunications business volume. By 2030, there will be 50 5G (including 5G-A) base stations per 10,000 people, intelligent computing power will reach 9,800 EFLOPS, and the 5G user penetration rate will reach 95 percent, the ministry said. EFLOPS, or ExaFLOPS, is a unit of computing performance, with each unit representing 1 quintillion floating-point operations per second. The plan lays out 26 key tasks across six major areas including information infrastructure construction as well as network and data security assurance. Among these, it specifically highlights the need to initiate 6G commercial services at an appropriate time and to accelerate the establishment of a nationwide integrated computing power network. Specific measures also include building an industry anti‑fraud laboratory and supporting enterprises to deeply promote the integration of artificial intelligence and manufacturing, the plan said. China has established the world's largest information infrastructure. Gigabit optical network access is available in every county, while 5G networks cover all towns and more than 95 percent of administrative villages. The country is pushing ahead with its Digital China initiative, aiming to raise the added value of the core industries of the digital economy to 12.5 percent of GDP by 2030, according to the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030).

item.title: Xi, Peng Liyuan visit Grand Egyptian Museum
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
CAIRO, Sept. 2 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, visited on Wednesday the Grand Egyptian Museum accompanied by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife. The two heads of state and their spouses took in the exquisite and imposing stone carvings and inscribed stone pillars. They then gazed out at the pyramids from the museum's observation deck. Entering the Tutankhamun exhibition hall, the two presidents viewed such prized treasures as the pharaoh's throne, the golden mask and royal chariots. Noting that China and Egypt are both ancient civilizations and countries rich in World Heritage sites, Xi said that across time and space, the two civilizations have been reaching out to each other, adding new chapters of everlasting friendship between the two peoples. Xi called on both sides to uphold the vision of civilization based on equality, mutual learning, dialogue and inclusiveness, and implement the Global Civilization Initiative. He also urged the two countries to promote the inclusive coexistence and mutual learning among different civilizations, and pool greater strength from civilizations to advance the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. Sisi thanked Xi for extending congratulations on the opening of the museum last year. He said the ancient Egyptian and Chinese civilizations share the qualities of openness, inclusiveness and harmonious coexistence amid diversity, which closely aligns with the vision of the Global Civilization Initiative proposed by Xi. The Egyptian side stands ready to work with China to step up people-to-people and cultural exchanges, promote mutual learning among civilizations, and make the world more harmonious and inclusive, Sisi said.

item.title: Xi calls for deepening China-Egypt cooperation, raises Mideast proposal
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
CAIRO, Sept. 2 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called on China and Egypt to support each other, deepen cooperation, and continue advancing the building of a China-Egypt community with a shared future amid a turbulent international and regional landscape. Xi made the remarks during his talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, while emphasizing China's support for regional countries in building a new security architecture in the Middle East via upholding a vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security. ENHANCING BILATERAL EXCHANGES, COOPERATION Noting that Egypt was the first Arab and African nation to establish diplomatic ties with the People's Republic of China in 1956, Xi said that the older-generation leaders of the two countries led their peoples in striving side by side for national independence and against imperialism and colonialism, forging an unbreakable bond of friendship. Over the past seven decades, China-Egypt relations have weathered challenges and developed distinctive features of equality and mutual trust, friendship and mutual learning, solidarity and mutual support, as well as win-win cooperation, he said. Xi said the China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership has achieved leapfrog development in recent years under the guidance of the two heads of state. The two sides share similar views and have closely aligned strategies in pursuing development and revitalization, improving people's well-being, and upholding international fairness and justice, he added. Xi emphasized that China and Egypt should firmly support each other, maintain the momentum of high-level exchanges, enhance exchanges and cooperation in all fields and at all levels, and strengthen exchanges and mutual learning on governance experience. Xi said the two sides should promote mutually beneficial cooperation, better align their development strategies, tap the potential for cooperation in traditional fields such as infrastructure development, power, agriculture and communications technology, and foster new highlights of cooperation in green energy, electric vehicles, aerospace, the digital economy and modern agricultural technology. The two sides should promote people-to-people exchanges, comprehensively expand exchanges and cooperation in culture, education, science and technology, health, sports and other fields, and facilitate personnel exchanges and enhance people-to-people bonds, Xi said. The two sides should strengthen security cooperation, jointly combat transnational crime, deepen international cooperation in anti-corruption, firmly support each other's anti-terror efforts, and safeguard their common security, Xi said. The two sides should strengthen multilateral collaboration, further enhance coordination and cooperation on multilateral platforms such as the United Nations and the BRICS, jointly promote the development of the China-Arab States Cooperation Forum and the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, jointly oppose unilateralism and acts of bullying, and promote a more just and equitable global governance system, Xi said. For his part, Sisi welcomed Xi's historic state visit to Egypt on the occasion of the 70th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two countries. Sisi said that since the establishment of diplomatic relations, bilateral ties have developed in a sound and steady manner, and cooperation across various fields has yielded fruitful results. Egypt firmly adheres to the one-China principle and is committed to further advancing the Egypt-China comprehensive strategic partnership, Sisi added. Egypt is ready to work with China to deepen cooperation in trade and investment, manufacturing, infrastructure development, finance, science and technology, and new energy, strengthen military and security exchanges, and promote closer people-to-people exchanges, so as to benefit the two peoples and contribute to regional development and prosperity, Sisi said. Sisi said China, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, plays an important and constructive role in international affairs. Egypt is ready to strengthen coordination with China at multilateral platforms, jointly address global challenges, and work together to uphold international fairness and justice, he added. The two heads of state jointly witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents on Belt and Road cooperation, artificial intelligence, economy and trade, and industrial and supply chain cooperation. The two sides also issued a joint statement on further deepening their comprehensive strategic partnership, and signed more than 20 cooperation documents covering such areas as digital economy, science and technology, education, and transportation. NEW REGIONAL SECURITY ARCHITECTURE In the talks, Xi raised a four-point proposal on building a new security architecture in the Middle East, saying that China supports countries in the region in developing good-neighborly and friendly relations. To promote common security in the region, Xi said that efforts should be made to foster the internal driving force for common security in the region. People in the Middle East should remain masters of their own affairs, and external interference should be rejected, Xi said, noting that China supports regional countries in strengthening dialogue on peace and security, exploring the building of a new security architecture for the Middle East, and taking their future into their own hands. Xi said that a comprehensive approach should be adopted to advance common security in the region and that given the multiple hotspots in the Middle East and their close interconnections, comprehensive solutions should be pursued. The Palestinian issue remains at the core of the Middle East question and should never be overlooked or marginalized, he added. The foundation for common security should be strengthened through development, Xi said, noting that lasting peace and stability in the Middle East fundamentally depend on development. China stands ready to work with Middle East countries to safeguard the security of international shipping lanes, advance development cooperation, promote the convergence of interests of regional countries, gradually enhance mutual trust, and eliminate the root causes of the conflict, he said. Xi urged that international coordination for common security in the region should be strengthened, and the UN Charter and international law should serve as the fundamental principles for handling Middle East affairs. The international community, especially external powers, should abandon double standards in the Middle East, respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of regional countries, and safeguard regional peace and stability, Xi added. He also urged support for the United Nations' effective role in Middle East affairs. Sisi said that Egypt highly appreciates China's consistent, objective, and impartial stance on the Middle East question, noting that Egypt is committed to promoting de-escalation in the region, resolving conflicts and differences through political means, and advancing regional security and development. Egypt stands ready to continue strengthening coordination with China to ease tensions in the Middle East, safeguard regional stability, and explore a regional security architecture, Sisi said.

item.title: China tightens accountability for officials regarding ecological, environmental damage
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 25 -- Chinese officials found responsible for serious ecological and environmental damage will be held accountable for life, even if they have since left their posts, according to a recently released policy document. Issued by the General Office of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council, the document outlines the cases that can lead to official accountability, as well as the disciplinary measures that may follow. The accountability framework was originally released in 2015. An official with the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee said an update was necessary as China has entered a stage of high-quality development featuring accelerated green and low-carbon growth, while the CPC Central Committee has issued a series of new requirements on ecological and environmental protection in recent years. The revised rules broaden the scope of accountability beyond leading Party and government officials to include senior officials at public institutions, development zones and state-owned enterprises. China has pledged to bring carbon dioxide emissions to a peak before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2060. The revised document specifies that local officials who fail to effectively advance these efforts will also be held accountable. Meanwhile, the official from the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee noted that accountability for ecological and environmental damage must be precise and evidence-based. "It should neither dampen officials' enthusiasm for work, nor undermine the credibility of the Party and the government." China has stepped up ecological and environmental protection efforts. During the second round of the central ecological and environmental protection inspections, conducted from May 2020 to June 2022, a total of 3,371 people were held accountable. The third round of such inspections is currently underway. The revised accountability rules also bring them into line with China's Ecological and Environmental Code, which officially took effect on Aug. 15.
